Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap + next steps from our side related to audit logging and compliance: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Redwood provides both admin activity logs (console/user actions, role changes, permission grants) and API request logs (request metadata, timestamps, client IPs, request/response sizes).
- Logs are available for real-time streaming to SIEMs (Splunk/Datadog) and bulk export to customer S3 buckets.
- We support configurable retention policies per account and can enable write-once/read-many (WORM) exports (S3 Object Lock) for immutability requests.
- SOC 2: we completed a readiness audit; Type II certification expected Q3 2026 (we can share current evidence and our controls summary now).

Attachments included:
- Redwood_AuditLogging_Specs.pdf (details on log schema, fields, and export mechanics)
- SOC2-Readiness-Summary.pdf (high-level controls & timeline)

Open items / asks for you
1) Please confirm whether you need full request/response bodies in API logs, or only metadata (timestamp, method, path, status, latency).
2) Can you share the vendor security questionnaire that your procurement team prefers (I can have our security team fill and return)? I attached a template placeholder — feel free to send yours and we'll prioritize.
3) If you plan to ingest logs into Splunk, any specific connector/version requirements? We can schedule a short engineering deep-dive.

Next steps from Redwood
- I'll loop in Aditya (solutions) for a technical deep-dive early next week.
- Our security team will start the vendor questionnaire as soon as we receive your XLSX.
- I've attached the audit logging spec & SOC2 readiness summary for your review.

Proposed times for the tech deep-dive: Wed 8/19 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 8/20 9:00-10:00 PT — let me know what works.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our security & infra teams: 

1) Exportability: we will be ingesting logs into Splunk. Can Redwood stream logs to Splunk HEC directly, or do we need to pull from S3? Any latency or batching constraints to be aware of?
2) Immutability: we need guarantee that audit exports are tamper-evident / WORM. Does Redwood provide a managed immutable audit store, or do you rely on S3 Object Lock + retention policies?
3) API logs content: our legal/regulatory teams will likely require request/response bodies for a subset of endpoints (search/ingest). Is that configurable per-route? What about PII redaction support at export time?
4) SOC 2: timeline and what evidence you can share now (control descriptions, latest report, or at least interim evidence).

I've attached our Vendor Security Questionnaire (attached as Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx). Could you have your security team start filling the sections on logging, encryption, and access controls by EOD Friday if possible?

Also — timeline: we're targeting a procurement decision by end of September, so any ability to accelerate the SOC2 evidence handoff would be helpful.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Security Operations, Acme Corp
samir.patel@acmecorp.com

Subject: Re: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up / next steps

Samir —

Great questions — I pulled together answers inline below and flagged items for Aditya / our security team to own where appropriate.

1) Exportability / Splunk ingestion- We support both streaming and S3 export:
  - Streaming: native Splunk HEC support via secure HTTPS endpoints; typical end-to-end latency is ~5-15s depending on batch size and connection.
  - S3 bulk export: near-real-time (1-5m) or daily bulk exports depending on configuration.
  - Action: Aditya can run a short proof-of-concept to confirm your Splunk setup and HEC token exchange.

2) Immutability- Options we can provide:
  - Managed WORM export: we can write exports to a Redundancy-backed immutable store we manage for enterprise customers (configurable retention + tamper evidence).
  - Customer-managed S3 Object Lock: we can push logs to your S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled; this is the most common pattern for customers who require long-term immutable retention.
  - We also provide signed manifest files for each export batch so you can validate integrity.
  - Action: Security to confirm legal/controls language in the questionnaire for the exact verbiage.

3) API logs / request bodies / redaction- 
  - By default we capture request/response metadata (method, path, status, latency, authenticated user, request id).
  - Request/response bodies can be included for specific routes on a per-account basis (configurable) — this is subject to privacy controls and must be requested in writing.
  - PII redaction: we offer export-time redaction rules (regex-based) and a processing pipeline that can mask fields before export. We recommend redaction at ingest if you want to avoid storing sensitive bodies in the primary logs.
  - Action: Please identify which endpoints you want bodies for and we'll propose a data-retention + redaction plan.

4) SOC 2 evidence & timeline- 
  - Redwood completed an internal readiness engagement and our control baseline is in place. We expect SOC 2 Type II to be issued by the end of Q3 2026 (final auditor report).
  - In the meantime, we can share: control descriptions, recent penetration test summary, encryption & key management architecture, and interim SOC 2 evidence (system inventory, access lists, change logs).
  - Action: I've attached our SOC2-Readiness-Summary. Our security team (cc'd: Neha) will start on your questionnaire; expect a first-pass return by Friday.

Proposed next steps
- Aditya to schedule a 30-45m technical deep-dive with your infra team this week (we're proposing Wed 8/19 10:00 PT).
- Security (Neha) to begin filling the vendor security questionnaire and return the first pass by EOD Friday.
- Marissa to share a short write-up on immutability options and retention SLA.

If that works I'll send calendar invites.

Best,
Marissa
